newsitem.title: SLOVAKIA: Slovak SAX index dips despite Nafta revival.
newsitem.headline: Slovak SAX index dips despite Nafta revival.

text.p: Slovak oil and gas storage firm Nafta continued to rebound on the Bratislava Stock Exchange (BSE) on Wednesday, but falls from steel-maker VSZ pulled the SAX index down 0.76 points to 167.24.
Nafta traded the biggest volume -- 2,500 shares on the BSE's main floor -- after Tuesday's 7,867 shares, rising 15 crowns to 1,225 crowns.
Traders said they saw the issue reviving after a year-long tradeless period.
"It seems Nafta is becoming an interesting investment," Peter Krutil of Creditanstalt said.
In 1996, the state's privatisation agency, the NPF, sold Nafta to a little-known group, called Druha Obchodna a.s., at a price below its market value.
In reaction to the move, trading in Nafta came to a virtual standstill while its price fell to the current 1,200 crown level, from some 2,400 crowns.
"We see a demand for Nafta rising again, as its downfall had emotional, rather than fundamental reasons," Krutil said.
However, the 16-share SAX index was pulled down by a 15-crown decline in the price of VSZ. VSZ closed at 640 crowns, on 73 shares.
"Generally, the market remains volatile on low volumes, allowing large price-jumps on relatively small blocks," Krutil said.
On Tuesday, VSZ's price was lifted by a 10,000-share block.
Overall, volume remained low, totalling 49,611 shares, after 96,165 shares traded on Tuesday, while turnover eased to 43.1 million crowns, from 50.54 million.
